chunk_map.heading: Close the ticket your team's way
Read the ticket for your bug
Read the conventions off the ticket
Write the close-out and send it

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 line 16: "Drop the ticket link after the colon." is the nearest miss; the colon is the prompt's own `Ticket:` line on the same slide, so it resolves in-chunk. L52 "The loop that started with a failing test" is arc-earned spine vocabulary (carve-out); L54 "The field rules" resolves to L52 "the conventions your team has been encoding". Harm (pointer to nothing) absent.

chunk 6 line 54: "The next exercise sweeps this whole session." is the nearest; it is a forward pointer by reading order with a claim, and the maintainer block carries the dated §33 accept-note. L35 names its link target by title.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 line 52: "The loop that started with a failing test closed." resolves to fix-tests-first, which the maintainer Arc block names as the exercise before this one; L7 "the bug you shipped" is the same session's PR. No dead beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal beat; muted read finds every setup verbed (L13, L27, L37)

rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 4 "Double-check the voice" line 43 is the thinnest slide (one bullet) but carries a full self-standing instruction: "Does the note sound like the ticket's other comments?". Not a wait-state.

chunk 5 line 45 "Reverse-engineer anything" is the header most at risk; L47-48 state that anything can be reverse-engineered and give the move. Chunk 6 "Two artefacts from one ticket" matches L52. No contradiction.

grep for 'Not X. Not Y.' constructions in body: 0. Nearest: L47 list "a codebase nobody documented, a CI pipeline, a config, an API..." is an enumeration inside a verbed sentence; L48 three imperatives each concrete (study, extract a .md file, use it as context). No superlative, no number+retraction, no abstraction stack, no empty-leg verb triplet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE 'compendium|firing|forcing|beat|surface' over body lines 1-55: 0 hits. 'connector' L35 is cleared by the maintainer accept-note (2026-08-18).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep '\*\*' over body lines 1-55: 4 hits, L3/5/7/9, all widget chrome (Time/What you do/What you build/The point); no bolded handle in bullets, matching the maintainer emphasis-budget note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: exercise is referenced from curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md and plan-mode-done-right.md (grep -rl close-the-ticket); derive-body-view reports slide_count 6 matching the 6 `##` chunks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js -> 'OK — 59 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.'; grep -c '^## Phase\|^## [0-9]' -> 0 (no hand-numbered headers).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js -> 'OK — 59 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.'; grep -niE 'below|above|earlier' over body -> 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: one link, L35 "[MCP and connectors](../trainings/.../mcp-and-connectors.md)": names the document in the link text so the sentence works stripped, no geometry. Review surface, never a gate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/close-the-ticket.md -> 'oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: headers L11/L20/L33/L41/L45 are imperatives; L50 "Two artefacts from one ticket" is a closing recap label, the nearest to a non-imperative, and the rule states not every header owes a claim. L45 was reworded verb-led in the pinned diff, consistent with the rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 line 52: "The loop that started with a failing test closed." is the nearest to an aphorism kicker; the rule's own calibration names this slide's recap as a non-violation and it closes the arc. L25 "The rules the agent proposes are for this bug and the ones after it." adds scope, not restatement.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: pinned diff changed only the L45 header ("Anything can be reverse-engineered" -> "Reverse-engineer anything"). Cover-the-body test: the header promises an instruction to reverse-engineer beyond the ticket; L47 (what can be inspected) and L48 (the move) both answer it; no bullet answers only the old header.
